stem: During flowering, a plant with predominantly pistillate flowers develops a small number of pollen-producing structures. Which description is the most defensible?
choices: The plant must be reclassified only from the seed package description
The structures can be disregarded because pistillate flowers prevent pollen production
The observation proves every plant of the cultivar will express the same way
The observation should be recorded as mixed or altered sex expression rather than ignored because most flowers are pistillate
rationale: Cannabis sex expression can be plastic. Observed pollen-producing structures should be documented even when most reproductive morphology is pistillate; one plant does not establish a universal cultivar outcome.
